overview: Hemp as a fibre crop you grow, shape and breed: indica, sativa and the hybrid of the two, sown on farmland and cut for the fibre that makes rope, string and paper.

1.0.3: A clump left to itself runs on its days of light and waits on no night.
A field lit however you like still goes to seed.
Counting nights is the business of a plant somebody raised.
Crossing two strains and taking the hybrid seed earns an advancement.
A hoe sweeps a field with Useful Hoe installed, taking what is done and leaving the rest.
The block tip fills a green bar as a plant grows.
1.0.2: The rope has an icon instead of a missing-texture cube.
The placed cord reads as rope: one lay running true down a hanging length, not stripes.
1.0.0: Hemp arrives: three strains grown from seed through their own days and nights.
Indica short and bushy, sativa tall and lanky, and a hybrid between them.
Pollen crosses between strains in flower.
Six hemp make rope you can climb and walk through.
Eight in a ring make a lead, and fibre goes on to string and paper.
